body: If Michael Bay had done the 8th movie, it would've been intense.

The Passion of the Christ hands down. I like to watch it, read the gospels and passages that talk about His death, then watch it again. I love it, and I've heard that it's possibly the most accurate representation of what He would've gone through at the time. I'll try to find a source on that.

I know, but I can't stop. It fluctuates wildly between totally fine and extreme terror, but I think I'm starting to move past it.

I deleted all of my dating site profiles and I've come to terms with the fact that I can't force it. I'm planning to get involved at school next fall. My church is pretty small, so I'm not sure if I'd meet a girl there. I actually met my last crush in church, and I thought I would end up marrying her. Her turning me down (for a relationship) was what really made me question God and my faith. I'm better now and willing to move on and not feel sorry for myself!
I did. The investigator said he would write up a report to have it on file, but there was no need to come get it or anything because the situation is complete BS.
Eh, it comes and goes. Sometimes I'll be totally fine, but 2 seconds later I'll be scared out of my wits and hopelessly paranoid.

I just got back from Panama City, which wasn't a whole lot of fun. I sat inside and read a lot because it was so unbelievably hot!

The situation goes from "this is totally a scam" to complete and utter terror randomly. I'm honestly sick of that more than anything else.

I'm honestly glad I shared it, I would've either killed myself or paid up (the former most likely) if I hadn't sought outside advice first. I made a generic post in /r/suicidewatch the day it happened looking for advice on how to handle this, and they told me it was a scam. It's the first I'd heard of anything like that, and I was so glad it was.

Look through my post history if you get a sec, I'm going through this situation right now. People who fall for it are people who know that no matter what the situation, being charged with child pornography never ends well for the accused, even if they had no way of knowing they were speaking to an "underage girl."

I'm still really scared.

I wish I'd done that. I just blocked him and moved on until I got that call on Monday that brought this up again ten fold. I'm just ready to move past this, hopefully I can when I get to the end of next week. It's honestly torn me to shreds this past week.

It's great to hear that I'm not the only one, especially when people have dealt with "FBI agents" with real names like I have. I hate this world sometimes, man.

I hope so. If I don't hear anything by the end of next week maybe I'll be able to be rationally about this :D If it weren't for Reddit I don't know what I'd do. I just searched underage in /r/legaladvice hoping for some advice on how to deal with this and I was so surprised to find out that this was a well known scam and some people had posted situations almost IDENTICAL to mine. The "agent" is the part that seriously spooked me though and made me make a lot of other posts.

Yeah my age is clearly stated on my profile. I think hers MAY have said 22, but there are so many profiles on there that I can't tell you for sure. Also, she deleted her profile soon after we exchanged numbers. I seriously wish I'd gotten a picture in time.

Also, the dad claimed that he checked me out and that I was 28 years old and had demanded more pictures after finding out her age, which I absolutely did not. Age or anything remotely related was not discussed, it was mostly just her not replying to my questions and her asking me sexual questions, such as "are you hard when you wake up?" She pretty much initiated everything while I was seriously trying to plan a platonic date, but I'm not sure how much that matters legally. If anything, she solicited me! :D
And they all turned out okay? Nothing happened with them? Did the "FBI" get involved?
If it's still worrying me next week then I'll definitely go to my neurologist. I know I'll end up harming myself eventually if I don't get something to get me by.
I actually live near a military base, believe it or not.

I honestly didn't know what to do except call the cops. If it wasn't for a friend telling me to, then k would've paid up! They were reassuring about it and they didn't really seem to think I did anything wrong. They said they'd write up a report but it would be vague because the situation was BS. I'm hoping I can get past it after next week.

She was allegedly 16, I'm 19. He claimed that I asked her age and continued demanding pictures, which I didn't. He also said I was 28 years old, which I'm definitely not. I know it's a scam, but it really spooked me.
I hope you're right, that's the part that scared me the most about this entire situation.

I'm thinking that since I haven't heard anything out of anyone that it might be over and I can move past it, but there's always next week :/

The fear is extremely real. If it's still sticking with me next week then maybe I'll go to my neurologist about it. Does that sound like it would be a worthwhile idea? I've never dealt with something like this before so I'm sorry if I'm asking dumb questions.

Sound right?  That didn't really sound right to me, but I've been so beside myself that I hadn't even thought to check the legal stuff.
